note: Independent rejudgment at HEAD ff3feee994 after 3249a93545 and 38fb0c08fe, replacing the weak verdict of 8be6ddfbed. draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi Section 3.1.3.1 (rfc/drafts/draft-ietf-bess-mup-safi.txt): "The Source Address Length has a fixed length of 1 octet.", "compute the number of remaining octets by subtracting, from the Length field in the MUP NLRI common header, the offset of the end of the Source Address measured from the start of the Route Type specific field", and "- < 0:   the mandatory fields exceed the declared Length; the NLRI is malformed; MUST be treated as Treat-as-withdraw." Producer at HEAD, types.go::parseBodyT1ST: ErrMUPTruncated when fewer than the 6 fixed octets (TEID, QFI, Endpoint Address Length) remain, when the Endpoint Address is short, when nothing remains for the Source Address Length octet (the draft-mpmz-bess-mup-safi-02 form), and when a non-zero Source Address is short; ValidateNLRI runs the same decode at ingress. (1) Asserts the draft, not the code: the parser units assert ErrorIs ErrMUPTruncated, the session units assert RFC 7606 treat-as-withdraw itself (ActionNone, the route leaves MP_REACH_NLRI, MP_UNREACH_NLRI is exactly the held generation K0 and decodable, siblings byte for byte). (2) Fails on non-compliance, at every bound inside parseBodyT1ST: TestMUPT1STFixedOctetsWithinLength (new) cuts the Length inside the TEID, before the QFI and before the Endpoint Address Length; TestMUPT1STSourceAddressWithinLength (new) gives Source Address Length 32 and two source octets. Each is followed by a whole second NLRI, so the body slice has capacity past its Length and a parser that skipped the bound reads the next route's octets: I traced that deleting len(rest) < fixedLen panics on rest[4] or rest[5] and deleting len(rest) < sourceOctets panics on rest[sourceOctets:], both red; the recorded mutants (line 314 and line 359 to false) confirm it. The endpoint cut and the -02 cut in TestMUPT1STMandatoryFieldsWithinLength go red under a lenient len(rest)==0 return or a deleted endpoint bound (read; their records are revert-to-panic only). TestMUPT1ST02TreatAsWithdraw (now tagged) and TestMUPMalformedT1STTreatAsWithdraw carry the -02 and endpoint cuts through the receive path. (3) Isolated: TEID 0x3039 non-zero, Endpoint and Source Address Lengths 32, following NLRI well formed, so only the truncation can fire. (4) Whole requirement: every cut that leaves the route key (RD, Prefix Length, Prefix) intact is tagged and discriminated, with both polarities: a route ending exactly at its Length parses with nothing left and exact TEID and endpoint, and a well-formed UPDATE comes back byte-identical. Reading taken, stated openly: a Length ending inside the RD or the prefix is also below zero by the letter, but Section 3.1.3 makes RD, Prefix Length and Prefix the route key, so such a route has no key to withdraw and Ze discards it (TestMUPUnkeyableMalformedT1STDiscardedNotRelayed, "RD overruns the Length"; TestMUPParseErrors for the shared RD and parsePrefixField bounds). Those units are untagged for this row and earn it no credit; the unkeyable class is judged as the discard ruling, not here. Polarity labels are inverted between packages (mup: positive = well formed parses; reactor: positive = malformed withdrawn) but each file holds a genuine conforming and violating pair. Untagged corroboration: tlv_applicability_test parses a T1ST with a 32-bit source address and TLVs. Implemented and tested for all keyable truncations.
